answer: Use device-bound identity: each agent registers one hardware-backed cipher key from a secure enclave, so one device yields one identity. On joining, it proves possession, the network checks the key against a trellis of seen devices, and duplicates are rejected before any reward. Creating N fakes needs N real devices at about $30 each plus setup time, so cost grows linearly with N, while an honest agent pays once. Limit: one knoll workshop pooling hardware could still pass, so cap one identity per device batch per epoch.
